findings.title: Other lazy-delegate accessors still NPE for a concurrently deleted group
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() was made null-safe, but the three getSubGroupsStream(search/first/max) overloads at lines 254-269 still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. LazyModel/modelSupplier returns null when the group has been deleted from the database after its CachedGroup was loaded, which is exactly the concurrent-deletion scenario this PR fixes, so calling any of these overloads on such a stale GroupAdapter still throws NullPointerException instead of degrading gracefully.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting no exceptions
findings.body: The test starts a reader thread that records failures in caughtExceptions, sets deletedAll=true after deleting the groups, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty at line 157 without joining the reader thread. The reader may still be inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...) at that moment and may record the very concurrent-deletion failure the test is meant to catch only after the assertion has passed, making the regression test able to pass spuriously; the unjoined non-daemon thread can also keep issuing requests into subsequent tests.

findings.title: Test does not guarantee the reader overlaps the deletions
findings.body: The reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() and the main thread immediately proceeds to delete all 100 groups with no latch or other synchronization confirming the reader has performed at least one groups() call before deletions begin. On a busy or single-core CI runner the reader may be scheduled only after deletions finish, in which case the test never exercises concurrent read-versus-delete access and cannot reproduce the original NPE.
